answer: In a market for pulse alerts from sensors along a river and across tundra, each agent reserves a six-hour service slot before the buyer reveals randomly timed checks. Payment is proportional to checks passed within the slot, with a fixed pool per site and missed checks forfeiting the reserved fee. A swarm of aliases sharing one operator cannot answer simultaneous probes without extra instruments and bandwidth; idle aliases earn nothing. Attackers with many real sensors can still compete, so sites need independent calibration and an appeal for faulty probes.
